source_evidence: Because these fees were far in excess of the brokers’ actual costs, FINRA found that the fees were actually disguised commissions that were not adequately disclosed.
answer: Miscellaneous fees are charges a broker may use to reimburse expenses connected with a transaction or service. But a fee labeled “handling” or another miscellaneous charge can function like a commission if it greatly exceeds the broker’s actual cost. The source describes FINRA finding that excessive handling fees were disguised commissions that had not been adequately disclosed. This example shows why it is useful to look beyond a fee’s label and consider its amount and explanation; not every high fee is necessarily a disguised commission.
